main_body: rectangular metal engine casing (rows 16-47) with two vertical exhaust pipes on top (rows 7-20) and a circular purple core on the front face
top_band: light blue-grey horizontal top surface of the main casing across rows 16-21 (row 16 back edge highlight, rows 17-20 flat top plane with a dark slot at row 19, row 21 front-edge highlight)
evidence: Reading a column near the center of the main engine body: rows 16-21 form a 6px-tall lighter horizontal top band bounded by a 1px front-edge highlight at row 21, followed by a 2px dark eave shadow at rows 22-23 and the vertical front face from rows 24-47 (26 rows total below the top band). Although the two top pipes have flat 2px caps, the main body volume clearly shows a foreshortened top surface and front face.

style.evidence: Compared against the Beodeul stall and well references, the engine is composed of large, uniform single-colour fills (the entire front casing at rows 24-46 is one flat grey tone with a rigid grid of single-pixel rivet dots, the pipes are unshaded vertical colour bands, and the central core is flat concentric rings) with only 3-4 tonal steps on the metal and a stark near-black line along the left and bottom edges.
